parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a national document/entry exposure with facility and custody restrictions, over a comparatively mild division. Foreign posts must refuse cases where document discrepancy casts 'reasonable doubt' on sex, with fraud/lifetime-ineligibility considered; the Supreme Court upheld M/F-only markers, and travellers report confiscated passports and stranded arrivals — a universal-exposure measure drawing advisories from 8+ governments. A federal order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities; 22 states restrict facilities and 4 criminalize some use, with one documented arrest and men's-ward detention. Federal corrections impose conversion-therapy-style policies. The division itself adds little: no statewide adult facility or care ban, municipal nondiscrimination covering 46%, active litigation with some orders enjoined, but no state recourse or hate-crime enhancement elsewhere.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 order ended X-markers and self-selection; Nov 2025 Supreme Court allowed the restriction. Feb 2025 cable tells officers to refuse where document discrepancy casts 'reasonable doubt' on sex and to consider fraud-based lifetime ineligibility. Travellers report passports confiscated or blocked, some stranded; 8+ governments issued advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiry; ACLU suit pending; legal-aid FAQ on document rules.
entry_documents.interaction: Home passport meets federal screening; refusal strands the traveller before any division-level protection applies.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections adopted conversion-therapy-style policies from 2026 (hair cutting, hormone removal, substituted psychiatric drugs); prisoner counts unpublished since 2025. Immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and sexual abuse. Elsewhere a trans woman was held 24h in a men's ward after a restroom arrest.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute; ongoing litigation over custody policies.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor detained (e.g., trespass in one of 4 states, or federal custody) is placed by birth sex under the same regime.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities. Mapped bans: 10 states cover all government buildings, 9 more schools plus some buildings, 3 schools-only; 4 states make some use a criminal offence; 6 extend to some private settings. One documented arrest under a bathroom law.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This division has no statewide adult facility ban; governor's facility-limit bid failed. 29 states plus capital district have no mapped ban; four municipalities (46% of population) bar identity discrimination including public accommodations.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Traveller in federal buildings or restrictive states faces exclusion; in this division's adult private settings exposure is low.

care_services.exposure: Division medical board's Aug 2025 draft would make under-18 transition care unprofessional conduct (not yet operative). Nationally, funding freezes, youth-care executive orders and 27-state minor care bans. Subpoenas of under-19 patient records.
care_services.protection: No statewide ban on adult gender-affirming care; adult care lawful in the division.
care_services.interaction: Travelling minor needing care faces division and federal barriers; an adult visitor's routine medication continuation is unresolved in the record.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal orders call youth care 'mutilation' and direct investigation of 'gender ideology'; May 2026 counterterrorism strategy names 'radically pro-transgender' groups; Dec 2025 rewards memo uses 'radical gender ideology'. 2025 poll: 66% back ASAB on documents, 69% back sports bans.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Rewards memo never uses gender ideology as a criterion; strategy states counterterrorism won't target mere disagreement; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises the severity and discovery probability of any police or bureaucratic encounter.

minors_guardians.exposure: Executive orders target minors' care and criminally contemplate teachers aiding social transition; division boards restricted trans girls' sports and advanced the youth-care draft; one district requires birth-sex bathrooms or nurse's office. Facility bans reach K-12 in many states.
minors_guardians.protection: Governor's single-sex facility limit for students failed; marriage and adoption recognition for married couples.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent with a trans minor visiting government-funded facilities or seeking youth care encounters both federal and division-level barriers.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Division hate-crime statute omits gender identity (no penalty enhancement); no state or, outside four municipalities, local nondiscrimination recourse for a visitor. No trans-specific violence count or general homicide rate supplied, so the rate is unknown.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; four municipal ordinances cover 46% of population including public accommodations.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: A visitor assaulted outside those municipalities relies on federal, not state, charging enhancements.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No inventory data on enforcement of the four municipal ordinances, on other districts adopting facility policies, or on police bias-crime guidance; document and facility rules continue to tighten (Feb 2026 template law elsewhere).
remedies_unknowns.protection: Multiple federal orders blocked or enjoined; passport suit pending; division sits above worst-law and do-not-travel tiers; municipal ordinances survive repeal attempts.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies vary sharply by state and by which federal order is in force at travel time.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A has universal birth-sex toilet exclusion with document checks and routinely rejected complaints. This dossier has comparable or worse document/entry exposure (refusal plus fraud referral, upheld by its Supreme Court) and federal facility exclusion, but the rated division lacks a statewide adult facility ban, has municipal accommodations protections covering 46%, and several federal orders are enjoined — so slightly above 0.35-A.

0.45-A: birth-sex bathroom rule in publicly funded buildings upheld, borders accept foreign passports, no presentation offence. Here borders do NOT simply accept — marker restrictions and refusal instructions are harsher than 0.45-A, and custody conversion-therapy policy adds severity; but this division adds no adult facility ban and municipal protections. Net comparable, marginally lower.

0.55-D has a service equality law, functioning courts, occasional refusals, no facility ban, documents accepted. This dossier is clearly lower: documents are a documented universal exposure with refusal and fraud referral, federal facility exclusion exists, and custody policy is hostile, none of which 0.55-D features.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller's operative regime is national, not divisional. Entry is the sharpest exposure: officers are instructed to refuse on sex-doubt grounds and may invoke fraud-based lifetime ineligibility, with stranded-traveller reports and foreign advisories confirming this is enforced, not paper. Federal facility exclusion and hostile federal custody practices follow her into buildings and, if detained, cells. The division softens only the local layer — no adult facility or care ban, municipal accommodations ordinances, active litigation — but it supplies no state hate-crime enhancement, no statewide nondiscrimination coverage, and no remedy for a visitor outside four municipalities. Absence of a division-level ban does not offset the enforced national document and facility regimes; combined they place this in the elevated-risk band.
